- Black Knight on c3 is actively centralized
- White King on f1 is somewhat exposed
- White Rook on c1 is on the back rank
- White just moved the King to f1

The breakthrough move is **Ne2+**! This is a royal fork:
- The Knight gives check to the King on f1
- Simultaneously, the Knight from e2 attacks the Rook on c1
- After the King moves (forced), Black captures the Rook with Nxc1, winning decisive material

The main line: 1...Ne2+ 2.Kg1 (or any King move) 2...Nxc1 and Black has won a full Rook.

**Coaching note:** Look for Knight moves from centralized squares that create multiple threats—especially checks combined with attacking undefended pieces. When your opponent's King moves away from the center, check if your Knight can exploit its unique jumping ability to fork the King and a Rook or Queen. This Knight fork won the game.
